speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Health (a) what are the Ministry's plans to encourage seniors to adopt an active ageing lifestyle; and (b) whether such plans include (i) collaborating with the People's Association to convert Residents' Network to Active Ageing Centres in the day and (ii) setting up volunteering opportunities for seniors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As explained to the House before, we have three inter-related healthcare systems and the aged care system is a key one we are prioritising for review.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Encouraging seniors to adopt active lifestyles and practice good health habits is the most sustainable and effective way to address the challenge of an ageing population with rapidly rising number of people with chronic and other illnesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To do so, we need to strengthen our ageing infrastructure in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Many of our initiatives are laid out in a recent 2023 Action Plan for Successful Ageing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: But AACs cannot work alone, and close collaboration with other agencies, such as the Health Promotion Board (HPB) and the People's Association (PA) will be critical and we seek the support of all Advisors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, to outreach to seniors more effectively and extensively, we need to tap on all community volunteers, whether they are from the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) or PA.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: To enable seniors to lead an active lifestyle, HPB and PA need to organise suitable activities, and be as inclusive as possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Promoting senior volunteerism will be an important thrust.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Health)
text: For example, the expansion of AACs will offer more volunteer roles such as buddying and befriending.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: With regards to my Parliamentary Question, I actually asked about whether we can convert the Residents' Network (RNs) into AACs, especially during the day.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: And I would like to ask will the Ministry possibly study this of converting such RNs to AACs and maybe study its impact on promoting active ageing for seniors.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My second question is in relation to setting up volunteering opportunities for our seniors, which the Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned earlier.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can she elaborate on what types of volunteering activities will be made available and how do we ensure these opportunities are suitable and accessible for the seniors of varying abilities?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are already in communication with PA to open up the spaces.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: It will really depend on the different areas because we are looking at where there are gaps, and we are trying to fill in those gaps.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: There will be key performance indicators (KPIs) to be achieved to see whether the AACs are keeping up with the outcomes that are targeted.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will definitely be working with PA and depending on the different areas, we will be working with the advisors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We look forward to Members' support on this.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: AACs are also volunteering opportunities for the seniors to organise the active ageing programmes for fellow seniors and reach out to those seniors who are in isolation.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We will continue to work with partners to ensure that there are a whole host of different types of volunteer activities that will be able to attract seniors with different abilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is indeed the problem that many of us face.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We do not have the monopoly on the ideas on this; in fact, that is why we are working very closely with partners, as well as with the different communities to understand what the different demographics or interest are.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Perhaps, with this collaboration with partners on the ground, we will be able to come up with activities that will attract these seniors.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: We are also trying to bring in these seniors to bring out their other friends, so perhaps, that is also one way to enhance participation from those who have not traditionally included themselves in these activities.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: She touched much on the help from volunteers and volunteer networks.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can I just weigh in to ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, is MOH confident of the current manpower resourcing, staff resourcing of our AACs, given their role that MOH has given them, as in charge of cluster support?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Particularly, they need to do extensive house visits to outreach to many units and a lot of these seniors may not be as amenable to their neighbours to visit the AACs on a regular basis.
